title: Algorithm for Gestational Age Assessment at Birth
author: Zilma Reis
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bawbifan

DetailsInsert data in the information system entries:

steps.title: Interview for Last Menstrual Period
steps.instruction: Conduct a structured interview with the woman using the following questions to obtain a reliable LMP reference:

substeps.instruction: 1. When did your last menstrual period occur? Confirm it was the first day of menstruation.
2. Are you sure about this date?
3. Are your menstrual cycles regular? Clarify that regularity means the cycle length did not change by more than one week.
4. Two months before your last menstrual period, did you use any contraceptive method (e.g., pills, injections, Mirena IUD, skin implant, vaginal ring)?
5. Two months before your last menstrual period, did you have an abortion or deliver a child?

steps.title: Photograph Prenatal Care Book LMP
steps.instruction: With the participant’s permission, take a clear picture of the personal prenatal care book page that records the LMP and verify that the date shown matches the interview response to avoid recall bias.

steps.title: Identify First Ultrasound CRL Record
steps.instruction: Locate the earliest obstetric ultrasound report performed between 7 weeks 0 days (7w+0d) and 13 weeks 6 days (13w+6d) of gestation; the crown‑rump‑length (CRL) measurement in this window is the primary reference.

steps.title: Record and Adjust Ultrasound CRL Data
steps.instruction: Chronologically organize all antenatal ultrasound reports, then:

substeps.instruction: a. Select the first assessment that includes a CRL measurement within 7w+0d–13w+6d.
b. Record the assessment date and the gestational age reported at that time.
c. If the reported gestational age is incomplete (e.g., 7/8 weeks), treat it as 7 weeks 3 days (7w+3d).
d. Note the CRL value (even if only visible in the embryo image).
e. Adjust the gestational age using the Intergrowth‑21st standard curve for CRL measurements applicable from 7 weeks 3 days to 13 weeks 6 days.

steps.title: Photograph Ultrasound Report
steps.instruction: With permission, capture a picture of the selected ultrasound report; if the report is unavailable, photograph the page of the prenatal care book where the ultrasound result is recorded.

steps.title: Run Automated Gestational Age Algorithm
steps.instruction: Enter the verified LMP information and the adjusted CRL‑based gestational age into the pre‑developed software, which applies the Intergrowth‑21st CRL reference and the reliable LMP criteria from the cited guidelines to compute the gestational age at birth.

steps.title: Expert Data Verification and Re‑calculation
steps.instruction: A team of expert researchers should:

substeps.instruction: a. Access the database together with the digital images of the ultrasound reports, CRL images, and prenatal care book scans.
b. Double‑check each newborn’s data against the original sources.
c. If discrepancies are found, adjust the gestational age to reflect the corrected information.
d. Re‑run the algorithm with any updated inputs to obtain the final optimal gestational age at birth.
